questions.stem:

• The student wants to emphasize both the scope and the principal finding of the study.
Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish the goal?

options.A: In 2018, researchers conducted a study, but the number of sites is not known.
options.B: Researchers in botany have studied many topics, including some unrelated to night-blooming flowers.

questions.explanation: The correct choice accurately combines the study’s scope and its principal finding in one concise sentence.

questions.stem: Researchers want to determine whether a new tutoring method causes higher algebra scores. They randomly assign 180 volunteer students to either the new method or the standard method and use the same final assessment for both groups. Which conclusion is best supported if the new-method group scores significantly higher?

options.A: The method will cause the same improvement for every student in the country.
options.B: The method and scores are associated, but random assignment provides no evidence about causation.
options.C: For students like those who volunteered, the tutoring method likely caused the difference in scores.
options.D: The standard method necessarily lowers scores below what students would earn with no tutoring.

questions.explanation: Random assignment supports a causal conclusion for participants like those in the study, but volunteer sampling limits broad generalization.
